questions.explanation: An automatic premium loan is not considered a Nonforfeiture Option.

questions.question: What advantage does the renewability feature give to a term policy?

options.label: A

options.label: C
options.text: The insured may borrow against the cash value

options.label: D
options.text: The insured may extend the coverage period

questions.question: The Common Disaster clause provides that if both the insured and the sole named beneficiary were to die in a common accident, which of the following is true?

options.label: A
options.text: This clause provides the payment of proceeds to the insured's estate

options.label: B

options.text: The estate taxes in the insured's estate may be reduced

options.label: D

questions.question: Tom has a qualified retirement plan with his employer that is currently considered to be 80% "vested". How can this be interpreted?

questions.question: Which of these is an element of a Variable Life policy?

questions.explanation: To determine the premium rate on a Whole Life policy, an insurance will consider the risk classification of the applicant.

questions.question: Which of the following does Social Security NOT provide benefits for?
questions.explanation: Social Security provides for all of these types of benefits EXCEPT dismemberment.

questions.question: Which of the following are Equity Indexed annuities typically invested in?

questions.question: A life insurance arrangement which circumvents insurable interest statutes is called:
questions.explanation: Investor-originated i'g insurance (or IOLl) is used to circumvent state insurable interest statutes. questions.question: An applicant who pays the initial premium at the time of application is typically given a(n)

questions.question: Which entity approves the insurance policy forms used in Florida?

questions.question: The investment gains from a Universal Life Policy usually go toward:

questions.question: The Consideration clause in a life insurance contract contains what pertinent information?

questions.question: A provision in a life insurance policy that pays the policyowner an amount that does not surpass the guaranteed cash value is called the:

questions.question: How can an agent-in-charge have more than one location?

questions.question: Which statement about a whole life policy is true?

questions.question: Which of the following is TRUE about a qualified retirement that is "top heavy"?

options.label: A
options.text: More than 30% of plan assets are in key employee accounts

questions.question: B receives yearly dividends and interest from a participating life insurance policy. Which of these should B include as gross income for federal income tax purposes?

options.label: D
options.text: Neither interest nor dividends are taxable

questions.question: Life and health insurance policies are:

questions.question: T is covered by an Accidental Death and Dismemberment (AD&D) policy that has an irrevocable beneficiary. What action will the insurance company take if T requests a change of beneficiary?

options.label: B
options.text: Change will be made only if premiums are paid current

options.text: Request of the change will be refused

questions.question: A Limited-Pay Life policy has:

options.text: Failing to acknowledge and act promptly with respect to an insurance claim

options.label: B
options.text: Compelling an insured to initiate a lawsuit by offering less on an insurance claim

options.label: C
options.text: Failing to accept or deny a claim within reasonable time after proof of loss is submitted

options.label: D
options.text: Needing written documentation of claim details

questions.explanation: All of these are unfair claim settlement practices except “Needing written documentation of claim details".

questions.question: Credit Life insurance is:

options.label: A
options.text: issued in any amount at the discretion of the applicant

options.label: B
options.text: used in the event of loss of income

options.label: C
options.text: issued in an amount not to exceed the amount of the loan

options.label: D
options.text: coverage that waives the premiums on a loan payment in the event of total disability

questions.explanation: Credit life insurance is designed to cover the life of a debtor and pay the amount due on a loan if the debtor dies before the loan is repaid.

questions.question: A Universal Life policy is sometimes referred to as an unbundled Life Policy because the owner can see the interest earned, expense charges, and the
questions.explanation: The Universal Life Policy is called an unbundled Life Policy because the policyholder can see the expense charges, the interest eamed, and the cost of insurance.

questions.question: W gave W's age as 50 when W purchased a Life policy. At the time of W's death seven years later, the company discovered W's true age at issue had been 59. What would the normal procedure be under the misstatement of age provision in regard to the payment of the death claim?

options.label: A
options.text: The policy's full death benefit would be paid, due to the expiration of the incontestable period

options.label: B
options.text: The proceeds would be reduced based on whatever the premium would have been if purchased at age 59

options.label: C
options.text: There would be no death proceeds paid out by the insurer

options.label: D
options.text: The insurer is only obligated to refund all premiums paid

questions.explanation: In this situation, the proceeds will be reduced based on whatever the premium would have been if purchased at age 59.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT considered to be an element of an insurance contract?
questions.explanation: The elements of an insurance contract do not include negotiating.

questions.question: If an agent combines premiums collected with their personal funds, they have engaged in:
questions.explanation: An agent who has combined premiums collected with personal funds has engaged in commingling, which is a prohibited.

questions.question: N is a 40-year old applicant who would like to retire at age 70. He is looking to buy a life insurance policy with level premiums, permanent protection, and be paid-up at retirement. Which of these should N purchase?
questions.explanation: Limited pay whole life policies have level premiums that are limited to a certain period.

questions.question: In an individual retirement account (IRA), rollover contributions are:
questions.explanation: Rollover contributions to an individual retirement account are unlimited by dollar amount.

questions.question: M has an insurance policy that also has an outstanding policy loan at the time of M's death. The insurer will deduct the outstanding loan balance from the:
questions.explanation: If not repaid by the time the insured dies, the loan balance and any interest accrued are deducted from the policy proceeds at the time of claim.

questions.question: A policy of adhesion can only be modified by whom?
questions.explanation: A policy of adhesion is best described as a policy which only the insurance company can modify

questions.question: Which of the following statements is CORRECT about an agent who is taking an insurance application?

options.label: A
options.text: The agent should avoid asking the applicant questions that may cause embarrassment

options.label: B
options.text: The agent should have the applicant initial any changes made on the application

options.label: C
options.text: The agent may allow a member of the applicant's immediate family to sign the application if the applicant is not available

options.label: D
options.text: The agent may answer routine questions on the application for the applicant

questions.explanation: An agent who is taking an insurance application should have the applicant initial any changes made on the application.

questions.question: S would like to use dividends from her life insurance policy to purchase paid-up additions. All of these would be factors that determine how much coverage can be purchased EXCEPT
questions.explanation: The age of the beneficiary is irrelevant in determining how much paid-up additions can be purchased.

questions.question: J chooses a monthly premium payment mode on his Whole Life insurance policy. Which of these statements is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: The gross premium is higher on a monthly payment mode as compared to being paid annually

options.label: B
options.text: The gross premium is lower on a monthly payment mode as compared to being paid annually

options.label: C
options.text: The cash value from a life policy paid on a monthly basis builds quicker than one paid on an annual basis

options.label: D
options.text: The face amount of a life policy paid on a monthly basis is higher than one paid on an annual basis

questions.explanation: A premium payment mode that is more frequent than an annual payment will result in a higher gross premium.

questions.question: A variable life insurance agent must be licensed and appointed as a life and variable contract agent, as well as a(n)
questions.explanation: An agent marketing variable life insurance must be licensed and appointed as a life and variable contract agent and a broker dealer.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a type of agent authority?
questions.explanation: The three types of agent authority include express, implied, and apparent authority.

questions.question: When is the face amount of a Whole Life policy paid?

options.label: A
options.text: At the policy's maturity date only

options.label: B
options.text: When the insured dies or at the policy's maturity date, whichever happens first

questions.explanation: The face amount of a Whole Life policy will be paid when the insured dies or on maturity of the policy, whichever occurs first.

questions.question: Additional coverage can be added to a Whole Life policy by adding a(n):
questions.explanation: A decreasing term rider can add additional coverage to a whole life policy.

questions.question: When an insurer issues a policy that refuses to cover certain risks, this is referred to as a(n):
questions.explanation: Exclusions are features of a life insurance policy stating that the policy will not cover certain risks.

questions.question: A life insurance policyowner would like to file a complaint against a life insurance agent. In Florida, the entity that oversees these complaints is called the
questions.explanation: The Office of Financial Regulation oversees complaints against life insurance agents and agencies selling life insurance products.

questions.question: A(n) _____ annuity pays benefits based on units rather than stated dollar amounts.
questions.explanation: A Variable annuity pays benefits based on units rather than specific dollar amounts.

questions.question: A policyowner is able to choose the frequency of premium payments through what policy feature?
questions.explanation: Premium mode is the feature that allows the policyowner to select the timing of premium payment, such as monthly.

questions.question: A level premium indicates:

options.label: A
options.text: the premium is fixed for a period stated in the contract, then becomes variable

options.label: B
options.text: the premium can only be changed with the consent of the insurer

options.label: C
options.text: the premium stays level until the policy's renewal date

options.label: D
options.text: the premium is fixed for the entire duration of the contract

questions.explanation: A level premium means that the premium remains fixed through the life of a policy.

questions.question: K's whole life insurance policy lapsed two months ago due to nonpayment. She would now like to reinstate the policy. All of these statements are correct about the policy's reinstatement EXCEPT

options.label: A
options.text: K must reinstate within a stated period

options.label: B
options.text: K must pay back interest and premiums

options.label: C
options.text: K will forfeit the right to use the automatic loan provision upon reinstatement

options.label: D
options.text: K must provide evidence of insurability

questions.explanation: All of these statements concerning reinstatement is correct EXCEPT "K will forfeit the right to use the automatic provision upon reinstatement'

questions.question: Which of these factors does NOT influence an applicant's need for life insurance?

options.label: C
options.text: Future educational costs of the dependents

questions.explanation: An individual's need for a death benefit for survivors is influenced by all of the following factors EXCEPT self-maintenance expenses.

questions.question: In order for a domestic, foreign, or alien insurance company to conduct business, it must be authorized by whom?

options.label: A
options.text: The National Association of Insurance Commissioners (NAIC)

options.label: B
options.text: The state where they are conducting business

options.label: C
options.text: The attorney general in the state where they are domiciled

questions.explanation: Domestic, foreign, or alien companies must be authorized by each state where they conduct business.

questions.question: Within how many days must a licensee notify the Department of Financial Services of a change in address?
questions.explanation: All licensees are required to notify the Department of Financial Services of a change in address within 30 days.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a nonforfeiture option?
questions.explanation: Reduced Paid-Up option" is an example of a nonforfeiture option.

questions.question: Under Florida law, a variable annuity policyowner must be notified of the accumulated value of the contract

options.label: A
options.text: only when requested by the policyowner

questions.explanation: A variable annuity policyholder must be informed at least once each year of the accumulated value of the contract during the premium payment period.

questions.question: K is insured under a Group Life insurance policy. K is considered to be a(n)
questions.explanation: Each person covered under a Group Life insurance policy is considered to be a certificate holder

questions.question: S is covered by a whole life policy. Which insurance product can cover his children?
questions.explanation: The means of providing life insurance on the children of a person who is covered by a life insurance policy is by a child term rider.

questions.question: A potential client, age 40, would like to purchase a Whole Life policy that will accumulate cash value at a faster rate in the early years of the policy. Which of these statements made by the producer would be correct?

options.label: A
options.text: Straight life accumulates faster than Limited-pay Life

options.label: B
options.text: 20-Pay Life accumulates cash value faster than Straight Life

options.label: C
options.text: Cash value accumulation of both 20-Pay Life and Straight Life depend on the insurer's financial rating

options.label: D
options.text: 20-Pay Life and Straight Life accumulate cash value at the same rate

questions.question: What group term life feature permits an individual to depart from the group and continue to be covered without providing evidence of insurability?
questions.explanation: The conversion privilege allows an individual to leave the group term plan and continue his or her insurance without providing evidence of insurability.

questions.question: All of these statements about the Waiver of Premium provision are correct, EXCEPT:

options.label: A
options.text: A waiting period must pass before becoming eligible for benefits

options.label: B
options.text: Waiver of Premium is available on both permanent and term insurance policies

options.label: C
options.text: Insured must be eligible for Social Security disability for claim to be accepted

options.label: D
options.text: Insured must be totally disabled to qualify

questions.explanation: Receiving Social Security disability benefits is not a requirement to be eligible for the Waiver of Premium.

questions.question: The provision that can be used to put an insurance policy back in force after it has lapsed due to nonpayment is called:
questions.explanation: In cases where a policyowner wishes to reinstate a lapsed policy, the reinstatement provision allows the policyowner to do so with some limitations.

questions.question: An applicant's medical information received from the Medical Information Bureau (MIB) may be furnished the:
questions.explanation: Information received from the Medical Information Bureau about a proposed insured may be released to the proposed insured's physician.

questions.question: D needs life insurance that provides coverage for only a limited amount of time while also paying the lowest possible premium. What kind of policy is needed?
questions.explanation: Life insurance written to cover a need for a specified period of time at the lowest premium is called level term insurance.

questions.question: The amount of monthly disability benefits payable under Social Security is affected by which of the following factors?

options.label: B
options.text: Amount of the benefits available from other sources

questions.explanation: The amount of the benefits available from other sources affects the amount of monthly disability benefits payable under Social Security.

questions.question: An example of false advertising would be

options.label: B
options.text: An insurer exaggerating its dividends in a magazine advertisement

options.label: C
options.text: An agent spending more than $25 on marketing gifts for a client

options.label: D
options.text: An insurer advertising in an insurance trade journal

questions.explanation: An insurance company may be judged guilty of false advertising if it exaggerates its dividends in a magazine advertisement.

questions.question: J is an agent who recently told a claimant that his rights might be impaired if he does not complete a release form within a specified time. What could this agent be found guilty of?
questions.explanation: In this situation, the agent may be guilty of coercion.

questions.question: Which of the following is TRUE if the owner of an IRA names their spouse as beneficiary, but then before any distributions are made?

options.label: C
options.text: The account can be rolled into the surviving spouse's IRA

options.label: D
options.text: Distributions will be received tax-free if surviving spouse is over age 59 1/2

options.label: E
options.text: Future distributions are payable to the owner's estate

questions.explanation: A surviving spouse who inherits IRA benefits or benefits from the deceased spouse's qualified plan is eligible to establish a rollover IRA in the surviving spouse's own name.

questions.question: All individuals covered under a group contract will receive a(n)
questions.explanation: A person who is insured within a group contract will be given a certificate.

questions.question: An individual working part-time has an annual income of $25,000. If this individual has an IRA, what is the maximum deductible IRA contribution allowable?
questions.explanation: In this situation, the maximum allowable contribution is $6,000.

questions.question: Which of these arrangements allows one to bypass insurable interest laws?
questions.explanation: Investor-originated life insurance (or IOLI), sometimes called stranger-originated life insurance (or STOLI) is used to circumvent state insurable interest statutes. This is done when an investor (or stranger) persuades an individual to take out life insurance specifically for the purpose of selling the policy to the investor. The investor compensates the insured and makes the premiums, then collects the death benefit when the insured dies.

questions.question: Which of these are NOT an example of a Nonforfeiture option?
questions.explanation: All of these are examples of Nonforfeiture options EXCEPT Life Income.

questions.question: T has a term policy that allows him to continue the coverage after expiration of the initial policy period. What type of term coverage is this?
questions.explanation: Renewable Term policies guarantee the insured the right to continue term coverage after expiration of the initial policy period.

questions.question: What type of insurance offers permanent life coverage with premiums that are payable for life?
questions.explanation: A policy that provides permanent life insurance with premiums payable for life is called whole life.

questions.question: A policyowner's rights are limited under which beneficiary designation?
questions.explanation: An irrevocable beneficiary designation requires the consent and signature of that named beneficiary before a change of beneficiary occurs.

questions.question: In order for coverage on a non-medical insurance application to take effect the same day, the producer must collect a signed application and

options.label: C
options.text: forward it immediately to the insurer

questions.explanation: Coverage begins on the day in which the producer collects the initial premium and has the applicant sign the life insurance contract..

questions.question: T is the policyowner for a Life Insurance policy with an Irrevocable beneficiary designation. If T wishes to change the beneficiary, T must obtain permission from the:
questions.explanation: An irrevocable designation may not be changed without the written consent of the beneficiary.

questions.question: Agents that have been licensed for less than six years must complete __ hours of continuing education every two years.
questions.explanation: Florida agents licensed less than six years are required to complete 24 hours of continuing education.

questions.question: Who has the option to renew a Renewable Term policy?
questions.explanation: Renewable Term Policy is renewable at the option of the insured.

questions.question: The policy summary contains specific information on all of the following, EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The policy summary contains specific information on the provisions, benefits, and coverage of the policy applied for. It does not contain information on agent commissions.

questions.question: Which of these statements is INCORRECT regarding the federal income tax treatment of life inrurance?

options.label: B
options.text: Premiums are normally not tax deductible

options.label: C
options.text: Cash dividends are normally not taxed

options.label: D
options.text: Entire cash surrender value is taxable

options.label: E
options.text: Proceeds are received tax-free if there is a named beneficiary

questions.explanation: The total cash surrender value is NOT taxable. The interest gained is taxable.

questions.question: M purchased an Accidental Death and Dismemberment (AD&D) policy and named his son as beneficiary. M has the right to change the beneficiary designation at anytime. What type of beneficiary is his son?
questions.explanation: With a revocable beneficiary designation, the policyowner may change the beneficiary at any time without notifying or getting permission from the beneficiary.

questions.question: A statement made by an insured in an insurance application that must be true to the best of one's knowledge and which becomes a part of the contract is known as:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is "a representation." A statement made by an insured in an insurance application that must be true to the best of one's knowledge and which becomes a part of the contract is a representation.

questions.question: The type of annuity that can be purchased with one monetary deposit is called a(n):
questions.explanation: An imediate annuity is purchased with one monetary deposit.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT considered to be a right given to a policyowner?

options.label: B
options.text: Modify a provision in the insurance contract

questions.explanation: Changing contract provisions is not a policyowner right.

questions.question: All of these Settlement options involve the systematic liquidation of the death proceeds in the event of the insured's death, EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The Interest Only option does NOT involve the systematic liquidation of the death proceeds.

questions.question: Which of these life insurance riders allows the applicant to have excess coverage?
questions.explanation: Term riders allow an applicant to have excess life insurance coverage.

questions.question: Which of these actions should a producer take when submitting an insurance application to an insurer?

options.label: A
options.text: Issue a binding receipt to applicant if no initial premium is submitted

options.label: B
options.text: Disclose to the applicant the amount of commissions to be eared on this transaction

options.label: C
options.text: Inform insurer of relevant information not included on the application

options.label: D
options.text: Arrange for a copy of the Attending Physician Statement (APS) to be sent to the producer

questions.explanation: One of the actions a producer should take when submitting an application is to advise the insurer of any other relevant information not contained in the application.

questions.question: How do life insurance companies handle cases where the insured commits suicide within the contract's stated Contestable period?

options.label: A
options.text: Claims are denied under the Suicide clause of the policy

options.label: B
options.text: Company pays twice the face amount under the double indemnity clause

options.label: D
options.text: Premiums are returned under the Consideration clause

questions.explanation: Claims are denied under the Suicide clause of the policy.

questions.question: K pays on a $20,000 20-Year Endowment policy for 10 years and dies from an automobile accident. How much will the insurance company pay the beneficiary?
questions.explanation: If the insured dies before the endowment's maturity, the policy's face value — also known as the "death benefit" — is paid in a lump sum to any beneficiaries.

questions.question: Under a Renewable Term policy,

options.label: A
options.text: the face amount is automatically adjusted at the time of renewal

options.label: B
options.text: evidence of insurability must be provided at each renewal

options.label: C
options.text: the renewal premium is calculated on the basis of the insured's attained age

options.label: D
options.text: a new application must be completed at each renewal

questions.explanation: Under a Renewable Term policy, the renewal premium is calculated on the basis of the insured's attained age.

questions.question: If a policyowner does not pay the premium by the due date, the

options.label: B
options.text: policyowner is automatically assessed a late charge

options.label: D
options.text: policyowner can make the premium payment during the grace period

questions.explanation: If a policyowner does not pay the premium by the due date, the premium may be paid during the grace period.

questions.question: What type of insurance company is domiciled in England, but conducts business in Florida?
questions.explanation: An insurance company that is domiciled in any country other than the United States is known as an alien insurance company.

questions.question: What would be an accurate definition of "controlled business:

options.label: A
options.text: Insurance business that is written on the agent's own life, property, or interests

options.label: B
options.text: Insurance business obtained by an agent through coercion, intimidation, or boycotting

options.label: C
options.text: Insurance business that is obtained through false advertising

options.label: D
options.text: Insurance business that is obtained by replacing an existing policy through misrepresentation

questions.explanation: “Controlled business" is insurance business that is written on the agent's own life, property, or interests.

questions.question: When an insurance application is taken by a producer, which of these statements is true?

options.label: A
options.text: The applicant should have an attorney present during the application process

options.label: B
options.text: Any changes made on the application require the applicant's initials

options.label: C
options.text: Any changes made on the application can later be initialed by the producer if the applicant is unavailable

options.label: D
options.text: The producer has the discretion to ask or not to ask any of the questions listed on the application

questions.explanation: The producer should have the applicant initial any changes made on the application.

questions.question: An individual covered under a Group Life insurance policy is considered to be a(n)
questions.explanation: Each person insured under a Group Life insurance policy is a certificate holder.

questions.question: S, age 40, is looking to buy a Life Insurance policy that will allow for increases or decreases in coverage as his needs change. The policy best suited for S would be
questions.explanation: Universal life insurance is characterized by flexible premiums and an adjustable death benefit.

questions.question: A(n) _____ Life pc offers the owner investment in products such as money-market funds, long-term bonds and equities.
questions.explanation: A Variable Life policy offers the owner investment in products such as money-market funds, long-term bonds, or equities.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT considered rebating?

options.label: A
options.text: Sharing commissions with an agent licensed in the same line of business

options.label: B
options.text: Returning premium to a client as an inducement for purchasing a policy

options.label: C
options.text: Giving something of value to an insured in exchange for their business

questions.explanation: Sharing commissions with other licensed agents is not considered rebating.

questions.question: Who is normally considered to be the owner of a 403(b) tax-sheltered annuity?
questions.explanation: The participating employee normally applies for and owns a 403(b) tax-sheltered annuity..

questions.question: In Florida, most life insurance policies have a contestability period of
questions.explanation: The maximum contestability period for most life insurance policies is 2 years.

questions.question: In Florida, which agency is responsible for the rehabilitation or liquidation of insurers?
questions.explanation: The Department of Financial Services (DFS) is responsible for the rehabilitation or liquidation of insurers when necessary.

questions.question: When can a policyowner change a revocable beneficiary?

options.label: B
options.text: After the consent of the current beneficiary

questions.explanation: With a revocable beneficiary designation, the policyowner may change the beneficiary at any time without notifying or getting permission from the beneficiary.

questions.question: T took out a $50,000 life insurance policy with an Accidental Death and Dismemberment rider. Five years later, T commits suicide. How much will the insurer pay?

options.label: A
options.text: The total premiums paid minus any policy loans

questions.explanation: The suicide occurred outside the Suicide clause period (normally 1-2 years), thus the face amount will be paid

questions.question: Which of the following statements is CORRECT regarding the tax treatment of a lump-sum payment paid to a life insurance policy's primary beneficiary?

options.label: A
options.text: The proceeds which exceed the amount paid in premiums are taxable

options.label: B
options.text: The proceeds are taxable only if the beneficiary's tax bracket has changed from the payout

options.label: C
options.text: All proceeds are considered taxable income in the year they are received

options.label: D
options.text: All proceeds are income tax free in the year they are received

questions.explanation: If a life insurance policy has a stated beneficiary, all the proceeds are income tax free in the year which they are received.

questions.question: A license may be denied, suspended, or revoked if the licensee

options.label: A
options.text: engages in replacement of an existing policy

options.label: C
options.text: does not meet a sales quota

questions.explanation: Being found guilty of misrepresentation may result in the Department of Financial Services denying, suspending, revoking, or not renewing any license.

questions.question: Which of these do NOT constitute policy delivery?

options.label: C
options.text: Policy delivered to the applicant by the agent

questions.explanation: All of these constitute delivery of the policy EXCEPT issuing a rated policy.

questions.question: Apolicyowner may generate taxable income from which of the following Dividend Options?
questions.explanation: While policy dividends are not taxable, any interest paid on them is taxable income in the year the interest is credited to the policy.

questions.question: If an agent would like to sell Variable annuities, which state examination must the agent pass?
questions.explanation: An agent who wants to sell Variable annuities must be licensed by the state which includes examinations in Life and Variable contracts.

questions.question: The free-look provision begins

options.label: A
options.text: upon the date of the sales presentation

options.label: B
options.text: upon receipt of the policy by the producer

options.label: C
options.text: upon receipt of the policy by the policyowner

options.label: D
options.text: upon the completion of the application

questions.explanation: When delivering the policy, the agent needs to explain that the free-look provision begins upon receipt of the policy by the policyowner.

questions.question: A life policy that contains a monthly mortality charge as well as self-directed investment choices is called a(n)
questions.explanation: Vanable Universal Life is comprised of monthly mortality charges and self directed investment choices.

questions.question: The cash value in a(n) ______ Life policy may fluctuate to reflect changing assumptions regarding mortality cost, interest, and expense factors.
questions.explanation: A Universal Life policy has a cash value that may fluctuate to reflect changing assumptions regarding mortality cost interest, and expense factors.

questions.question: How long does the coverage normally remain on a limited-pay life policy?

options.label: D
options.text: at the discretion of the insurer

questions.explanation: Even though the premium payments are limited to a certain period, the insurance protection extends until the insured's death, or to age 100.

questions.question: A licensed agent must be appointed by an insurance company to solicit insurance in Florida. The agent's license will terminate if a certain period of time elapses without being appointed. How long is this period of time?
questions.explanation: An agent's license will terminate if the agent allows 48 months to elapse without being appointed for the class or classes of insurance listed on the license.

questions.question: Dividends paid from a life insurance policy are

options.label: D
options.text: issued by the Department of Insurance

questions.explanation: Dividends paid from a life insurance policy are issued by the insurer.

questions.question: P died five years after purchasing a life policy. While investigating the claim, the insurer discovered material misrepresentations made by P during the application process. Which of these actions will the insurer take?

options.label: A
options.text: Beneficiary will be denied the claim

options.label: B
options.text: Beneficiary will be denied the claim and refunded all paid premiums

options.label: C
options.text: Beneficiary will be paid the Death Benefit

options.label: D
options.text: Beneficiary will be paid a partial Death Benefit

questions.explanation: The incontestable clause prevents the insurer from canceling the contract even for a material misrepresentation.

questions.question: Which of the following professional organizations has its code of ethics incorporated into Florida law?

options.label: C
options.text: National Association of Insurance and Financial Advisors (NAIFA)

options.label: D
options.text: The American College of Life Insurance

questions.explanation: The professional organization whose code of ethics is incorporated into Florida law, and whose responsibility is to establish the activities of agents is the National Association of Insurance and Financial Advisors.

questions.question: K is shopping for a permanent life insurance policy that will offer her the MOST protection per dollar of annual premium. Which of these policies best fits her needs?
questions.explanation: Straight life insurance policies provide an insured the greatest amount of permanent protection per dollar of annual premium.

questions.question: Under an Interest Sensitive Whole Life policy,

options.label: A
options.text: premiums are determined by the policyowner

options.label: C
options.text: the policy normally renews every 10 years

options.label: D
options.text: cash values are determined by interest rates

questions.explanation: Under an Interest Sensitive Whole Life policy, the cash value accrues according to market value, except in the case of some companies which offer a guaranteed interest rate independent of markets

questions.question: Which Federal law allows an insurer to obtain an inspection report on a potential insured?
questions.explanation: The Fair Credit Reporting Act of 1970, or FRA, established procedures for the collection and disclosure of information obtained on consumers through investigation and credit reports.

questions.question: S buys a $50,000 whole life policy with a $50,000 Accidental Death and Dismemberment rider. S dies 1 year later of natural causes. How much will the insurer pay the beneficiary?

options.label: C
options.text: Refund of premiums paid plus interest

options.label: D
options.text: No claim will be paid because cause of death was from natural causes

questions.explanation: In this situation, the beneficiary is entitled to receive $50,000.

questions.question: The minimum age at which a person can sign a life insurance application is
questions.explanation: A person 15 years or older may contract for life insurance on his/her own life.

questions.question: Which of these statements concerning an Individual Straight Life annuity is accurate?

options.label: A
options.text: Life expectancy of the annuitant is not a factor

options.label: C
options.text: Only available to employees of nonprofit charitable, educational, and religious organizations

options.label: D
options.text: Payments are made to an annuitant for life

questions.explanation: A Straight Life annuity pays for the life of the annuitant.

questions.question: Traditional individual retirement annuity (IRA) distributions must start by:

options.label: C
options.text: April 1st of the year following the year the participant attains age 59 1/2

options.label: D
options.text: April 1st of the year following the year the participant attains age 70 1/2

questions.explanation: Distributions from a traditional IRA must be made by April 1 following the year the participant tums age 70 1/2 or an excise tax will be assessed.

questions.question: Which of the following situations are NOT subject to Florida life insurance laws?

options.label: B
options.text: Insurance companies’ life policy replacement requirements

options.label: C
options.text: Insurance companies’ setting of life insurance policy rates
